acceptance: Measured baseline from make ci-usage-report: Trunk queue time (created to first job started) median and p90 per run over 14 days, and the number of times more than 3 runs were pending
A proposal that keeps an exact-commit Trunk push run for every develop commit, with the expected queue reduction and risks to release admission and culprit naming
Owner decision recorded before any workflow change; if approved, the change lands and the 14-day queue p90 falls versus the baseline
context:
DONE 2026-10-26 (owner decision: close now — fast-job fix solved the backlog): once PR #3462 (00698603b) took effect on Trunk, the 24-run backlog drained completely. Across the latest completed Trunk runs (40375131609, 40378481946, 40384677507, 40386745519), queue wait time was 0.0 min on all four and fast-job duration was 7.9, 12.1, 12.0, and 12.2 min (12 consecutive green Trunk runs). Owner decided to keep serial Trunk (which protects PR CI from pool contention) and close without waiting for 2026-11-02.

OWNER DECISION 2026-10-25: no workflow change now. Re-measure the 14-day baseline once 7 days of Trunk runs use the fixed fast job (from 2026-11-02), then decide on lanes only if p90 is still high. Lane prerequisites are filed as trunk-concurrent-runs-prerequisites-20261025.

STUDY 2026-10-25 (514 Trunk push runs, 2026-10-11 to 10-25 19:00Z): queue time (created to first job started) median 22.7 min, p90 179.9 min, max 351 min; waiting for the first runner is only median 0.1 min, p90 2.2 min. Result latency median 43.1 min, p90 202.3 min. More than 3 runs pending in 40 episodes (16% of the time). Of total run time, 73.5% is waiting behind other Trunk runs, 24.2% jobs running, 2.2% waiting for a pool runner. On 2026-10-25 the fast job's median doubled from about 10 to 20.9 min starting exactly at 112979a75 (#3423, fixed by #3462 at 00698603b); with 76 develop pushes that day, this explains the backlog of up to 24 pending runs. No Trunk job needs ordering across commits: artifacts are SHA-named and run-scoped, dist-artifact binds to its own run, and release admission finds the exact-commit run by SHA. Order-dependent consumers: red_streak_start (culprit naming, arm gate, trunk-revert) could name a newer commit for one run's duration while an older run is in progress (fix: report 'culprit undetermined'); site-inputs.yml keeps one pending run (needs queue: max or an ancestry check); ci.yml:1215 calls trunk.yml, so a group change must be push-only. Modelled one week (Oct 18-24): Trunk queue p90 104-156 min serial; 28-77 min with 2 lanes (PR CI job wait +21%); 15-45 min with 3 lanes (+28-36%); 10-25 min with no group (+32-48%). Fixing the fast regression alone gives a modelled median 57 to 18 min and p90 158 to 104 min at no PR cost. Total Trunk job time is unchanged at about 2,170 runner-min/day in every option. Not modelled: paid larger runners for Trunk.

Source: observed 2026-10-25 while waiting for the Trunk run on the changelog cutover merge commit (run 40174662295, created 07:56 UTC, started after about an hour). Owner asked to track it the same day.
description: trunk.yml runs one at a time on develop (`concurrency` group per ref with `queue: max` and no cancelling), so during merge bursts results queue up: on 2026-10-25 six Trunk runs were pending at once and the run for the changelog cutover merge waited about an hour before starting. Per-commit runs are required: release admission needs the exact-commit Trunk push run and its dist-artifact, and the arm gate names culprits from Trunk runs. Find safe ways to cut the wait while keeping every commit tested, for example letting independent Trunk jobs of different commits run concurrently where they share no state, splitting the serialized part to only what needs ordering, or faster runners for Trunk only.
